title: Fibre-assassin containment in an open is invariant under arbitrary base change
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a locally finite type morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $F$ be a quasi-coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module of finite type [pqf-def-coherent], and let $U\subseteq X$ be an open subscheme [def-weil-open-immersion]. For any morphism of schemes $h:S'\to S$, put $X'=X\times_SS'$ [def-pc-base-change], let $h_X:X'\to X$ be the projection, and put $F'=h_X^*F$ [def-pc-module-pullback] and $U'=h_X^{-1}(U)$. If $s'\in S'$ maps to $s\in S$, then $$\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(F_s)\subseteq |U_s|\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{Ass}_{X'_{s'}}(F'_{s'})\subseteq |U'_{s'}|.$$ Associated points and the tensor pullbacks to scheme-theoretic fibres are as in [def-trf-relative-assassin]. No flatness or finiteness hypothesis on $h$ is imposed.

proof.text: Write $i_s:X_s\to X$ and $i_{s'}:X'_{s'}\to X'$ for the fibre projections. By [def-pc-scheme-fibre] they identify the fibre point sets with the points over $s$ and $s'$. The restriction of $h_X$ therefore gives a map $\rho:|X'_{s'}|\to|X_s|$. By [def-trf-relative-assassin], membership in the associated-point set of either fibre is precisely membership of its image in the corresponding relative assassin. Since $U'=h_X^{-1}(U)$, a fibre point $z'$ belongs to $U'_{s'}$ if and only if $\rho(z')\in U_s$.

Assume $\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(F_s)\subseteq U_s$ and take $z'\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X'_{s'}}(F'_{s'})$. Apply [lem-trf-relative-assassin-base-change] to $f,F,h$ and $z'$. Its forward implication gives $\rho(z')\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(F_s)$, using step 1 to read relative membership in the fibre. Thus $\rho(z')\in U_s$, and step 1 gives $z'\in U'_{s'}$. This proves the forward containment. The cited lemma requires only local finite type of $f$ and quasi-coherence of $F$, both among our hypotheses.

proof.text: For any $z\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(F_s)$ put $k=\kappa(s)$, $k'=\kappa(s')$ and $E=\kappa(z)$. By [lem-trf-relative-assassin-base-change] the residual fibre over $z$ is $\operatorname{Spec}B$, where $B=k'\otimes_kE$. The two factors are field extensions of $k$, so [lem-weil-common-extension-fields-tensor-nontrivial] gives $B\ne0$. Its zero ideal is proper; [lem-weil-pbc-minimal-prime-over-proper-ideal] gives a minimal prime $\mathfrak q$ over zero. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-irreducible-components-minimal-primes], $V(\mathfrak q)$ is an irreducible component of $\operatorname{Spec}B$. The point $\mathfrak q$ is its generic point: a closed set $V(I)$ contains $\mathfrak q$ exactly when $I\subseteq\mathfrak q$, so the intersection of all such closed sets is $V(\mathfrak q)$. Consequently there exists a residual-fibre component generic point $z'$ above $z$.

source.place: Tag 05DC, statement and proof, residual fibre; Algebra Tags 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), (3)-(4), and 00ES (lemma-irreducible), (1),(3).

proof.text: Now assume $\operatorname{Ass}_{X'_{s'}}(F'_{s'})\subseteq U'_{s'}$. For any $z\in\operatorname{Ass}_{X_s}(F_s)$ choose the residual generic point $z'$ from step 3. The reverse implication of [lem-trf-relative-assassin-base-change] says $z'$ belongs to the relative assassin upstairs, hence to $\operatorname{Ass}_{X'_{s'}}(F'_{s'})$ by step 1. Our assumption puts $z'$ in $U'_{s'}$; step 1 then puts $z=\rho(z')$ in $U_s$. This proves the reverse containment. The argument also covers an empty associated-point set, and uses no property of $h$ beyond being a scheme morphism.

lean.statement: theorem associatedPoints_fiber_subset_open_iff_baseChange {X S S' : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) [LocallyOfFiniteType f] (F : X.Modules) (hF : F.IsQuasiCoherentFiniteType) (U : X.Opens) (h : S' ⟶ S) (s' : S') : associatedPoints ((tensorPullback (f.fiberι (h s'))).obj F) ⊆ (f.fiberι (h s')) ⁻¹' (U : Set X) ↔ associatedPoints ((tensorPullback ((pullback.snd f h).fiberι s')).obj ((tensorPullback (pullback.fst f h)).obj F)) ⊆ ((pullback.snd f h).fiberι s') ⁻¹' ((pullback.fst f h) ⁻¹' (U : Set X))
